newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Philippines sees Jan mining licence restart.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Philippines sees Jan mining licence restart.

text.p: The Philippine government expects to be ready to restart granting mining licences from January after final alterations to mining regulations forced by an accident at the Marcopper copper mine in March, a senior Philippines official official said on Wednesday.

"In January, when we have completed the negotiations for the generic agreements, we will be able to grant FDAAs (mining licences), because it (new mining) has been made socially and politically acceptable to our people," Philippines Undersecretary for the Department of the Environment, Antonio La Vina, told a mining seminar in Melbourne.
La Vina said new rules relaxing restrictions on foreign mining investment were passed in 1995 and led to some new licences being granted.
However, the granting of new licences was put on hold after a tailings dam leak at the Marcopper Mining Corp mine while rules were revamped to include environmental safeguards.
La Vina said the process of including the safeguards meant the public was now more confident about allowing new mines and new foreign mining investment.
Three mining executives have been charged over the leak, which resulted in mine waste escaping into a river.
La Vina is attending Australia's National Trade and Investment Outlook conference.
The seminar was part of the conference.
